raised.claim: `guardHits` is only logged when the LLM omits batch IDs from `analysis.verdicts`, so guard rejections on a full verdict set are never logged.
raised.why_it_breaks: `covered` counts distinct in-batch `beer_id`s present in the raw `analysis.verdicts` before `planTriageActions` runs. When the LLM returns a verdict for every orphan in the batch (`covered === orphans.length`) and guards reject or degrade verdicts (`plan.skipped > 0` or `guardHits` non-zero), `covered < orphans.length` is false and the warning containing `guardHits` is never emitted.

raised.claim: Verdicts degraded to `matcher_bug` by Guard 3 are counted as `wontfix` in the triage outcome and daily digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: When Guard 3 rejects an unprobed `not_on_untappd` verdict, `planTriageActions` rewrites its `review_class` to `'matcher_bug'` and pushes it into `plan.quiet`. The loop over `plan.quiet` assumes only `'not_on_untappd'` and `'wontfix'` exist in `quiet`, so every degraded `'matcher_bug'` (and any unverified/unreferenced actionable verdict in `quiet`) increments `outcome.wontfix`.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: If the LLM includes a ```triage-scope fence in `issue.body` (imitating the open issues shown in the prompt), `parseScopeBlock` will parse the model's prose block instead of the appended block.
raised.why_it_breaks: `buildTriagePrompt` feeds open issue bodies—including their rendered ```` ```triage-scope ```` blocks—into the prompt. If the model mimics that format in `new_issues[].body`, `renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)` is appended after `issue.body`, and `BLOCK_RE.exec(body)` in `parseScopeBlock` matches the first occurrence in the string (the unvalidated block inside `issue.body`) rather than the authoritative block at the end.

raised.claim: Guard 4 does not account for rows attached earlier in the same batch, and Guard 2 is not enforced when attaching verdicts to `new_issues`.
raised.why_it_breaks: 1) `target.postCreationRows` is never incremented (or combined with `byIssue.get(target.number)?.length ?? 0`) as verdicts are accepted, so an issue at 11 rows can accept up to 50 more rows in a single run without tripping `MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE` (12). 2) In the `else` branch (`new_issue_key`), `rowSatisfiesScope` is not checked against the proposed issue's `scope`, allowing the LLM to attach rows in the initial batch that contradict the new issue's own `scope`.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: `recordEnrichFailure` resets `review_class`, `review_note`, and `reviewed_at` when `candidates_count` crosses the `0 <-> >0` boundary, but leaves `issue_number` populated.
raised.why_it_breaks: When a previously triaged failure crosses from `candidates_count = 0` to `> 0` (or vice versa), `recordEnrichFailure` clears the review fields so the row re-enters the untriaged pool, but `issue_number` retains the stale issue reference in SQLite while `review_class` is `NULL`.
